title: Autonomous Coding Agent And Sandbox Execution Roadmap
goal: Make Odysseus able to accept a bounded coding task, create an isolated worktree, run checks in a disposable Podman sandbox, collect redacted evidence, and prepare reviewed publish steps without broad host-shell access.

current_evidence.local_status: Coding-agent worker, sandbox bridge, evidence storage, Telegram coding intent and local E2E dry-run are implemented. Commit 64220ad3 adds a narrow homeserver SSH host-runner backend so Odysseus does not need Podman inside the app container or a broad Podman socket. The final Debian live smoke is currently blocked by homeserver access: SSH returns Permission denied and HTTP /api/version is unreachable from Codex.

target_flows.request_example: open a workstation/project-runner roadmap slice for Projekt X, implement Feature Y, run checks, then expose status for remote control
expected_flow: Workstation, project runner or roadmap runner creates a trusted coding-task plan with repo_id, objective, allowed paths and checks.
Coding agent builds a gated task plan and isolated worktree.
Sandbox worker runs allowlisted checks in a disposable Podman job.
Result observer stores redacted logs, exit status and artifact manifest.
Quality and done gates produce a reviewed handoff or publish plan.
Telegram can report status, blockers and next human decision and can request pause, resume or cancel without leaking secrets.
Telegram reads the same redacted task ledger as the workstation.
Telegram writes only safe control events, never raw task content, host paths or secrets.
The coding runner treats Telegram as operator input, not as the only task source.

target_flows.request_example: teste die lokale Seite visuell und pruefe Konsole/Netzwerk
expected_flow: Browser smoke runs in a no-GPU sandbox with bounded network policy.
Screenshots, DOM, console and network summaries are captured as redacted artifacts.
Quality gate can consume those artifacts as evidence.

non_goals: No new UI or placement decisions; UI agent owns presentation later.
No Docker MCP, Docker-only design or broad container-control MCP.
No arbitrary shell prompt, shell=True, host PowerShell, SSH or systemctl exposure to the agent.
No automatic commit, push, deploy or Cloudflare exposure without explicit operator gates.
No persistence of tokens, chat ids, private raw documents, private prompts, full logs or absolute host paths.
No fullweb sandbox network by default; web access must be allowlisted and bounded.
stop_rules: Stop if unrelated staged files are present or a hotfile conflict appears, especially static/frontpage-v2/app.js.
Stop if any slice would persist secrets, tokens, chat ids, private content or absolute host paths.
Stop if implementation would require destructive git, force push, reset or checkout rewrite.
Stop if live Podman, Telegram, network, deploy, commit or push action is needed but not explicitly granted.
Stop if sandbox execution would require broad host mounts or unrestricted network.
Stop if focused tests fail and the fix would leave the slice scope.

slice_queue.goal: Add a persistent redacted sandbox job ledger for submit/status/cancel/artifact events under data-safe paths.
slice_queue.done_when: Ledger stores job metadata, state transitions, hashes, artifact refs and redacted previews without raw private content or absolute host paths.

slice_queue.goal: Implement a sandbox worker core that validates jobs, renders Podman plans, supports dry-run by default and exposes submit/status/cancel/artifacts contracts.
slice_queue.done_when: Worker can submit dry-run jobs, reject unsafe requests, record ledger events and return redacted status/artifact manifests.

slice_queue.goal: Expose admin-protected sandbox worker routes for submit/status/cancel/artifacts and keep live execution disabled by default.
slice_queue.done_when: Routes require admin, redact outputs, do not execute live unless a live flag and operator gate are both present, and never expose raw host paths.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented routes/sandbox_worker_routes.py, registered in app.py and covered by tests/test_sandbox_worker_routes.py.

slice_queue.goal: Connect coding-agent task plans to sandbox jobs so quality checks can be dispatched through the worker instead of direct host subprocess by default.
slice_queue.done_when: Coding task plans can produce sandbox job requests from allowlisted checks, consume worker statuses and build quality gate reports from sandbox evidence.

slice_queue.goal: Standardize sandbox artifacts for logs, test reports, screenshots, DOM/console/network summaries and generated files.
slice_queue.done_when: Each artifact has kind, hash, size, retention, redaction flag, correlation id and safe relative ref; generated files require review.
slice_queue.evidence: Extended sandbox artifact policy with content_hash/correlation_id and browser/test artifact kinds.

slice_queue.goal: Add a per-job network policy model for none, bounded allowlist and blocked fullweb modes.
slice_queue.done_when: Sandbox jobs default to network none, allowlist jobs carry bounded host/domain metadata, and fullweb stays blocked without separate live gate.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/sandbox_network_policy.py and wired it into sandbox contracts/resource guard.

slice_queue.goal: Teach Telegram task orchestration to recognize coding tasks as optional remote input, report sandbox progress and ask for the next human decision when gates block progress.
slice_queue.done_when: Telegram can create and track a coding task intent without executing live work, and replies with concise redacted status, blocker and recommended next decision.
slice_queue.evidence: Extended Telegram workflow and task intent detection for coding_agent_task.

slice_queue.goal: Convert completed sandbox/coding task summaries into Memory/RaptorGraph write intents with source-linked provenance and model stamps.
slice_queue.done_when: Successful coding tasks can create reviewed knowledge candidates without storing raw logs, raw diffs or private content.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/coding_agent_memory_bridge.py with Memory/RaptorGraph candidate tests.

slice_queue.goal: Move live evidence and sandbox reports to durable mounted data paths so deploys/rebuilds do not erase proof artifacts.

path_groups.completion_criteria: Sandbox jobs have durable lifecycle state, admin routes, dry-run default and one approved Debian live proof.
Coding-agent checks dispatch through sandbox contracts and a dry-run e2e proves the whole backend flow.
Telegram can create, track and report coding tasks with redacted status and human-decision gates.
Evidence is durable, redacted and optionally convertible to reviewed Memory/RaptorGraph write intents.
Network and resource policy is explicit per job and unsafe modes are gated.

go_language.go: Proceed with the named slice and its allowed paths only.
go_language.partial: Complete safe repo-only preparation and leave live/design gates queued.
go_language.no_go: Do not execute the slice; record the blocker and move to the next safe slice.
go_language.deferred: Park the slice because it needs live Go, design placement or operator wording.
go_language.blocked: Stop because proceeding would risk secrets, unrelated worktree changes, destructive git or unbounded execution.
